installCommand.label: Install command
installCommand.explain: Rampa builds the command with a fresh bootstrap token. Viewing the command doesn't rotate the cluster token: an agent that's already installed stays connected.
installCommand.oneTime: This command contains a single-use token that expires in 2 hours. Paste it on the machine or cluster for {{name}} before it expires; if it expires or you've already used it, generate another one.

infra.description: Rampa creates the infrastructure in your cloud with OpenTofu and keeps a record of every run.
infra.emptyDescription: Create a cluster or a machine with k3s in one click: Rampa brings up the infrastructure and the agent in your account.

dashboard.noClustersDescription: Connect a cloud account and create a cluster or a machine to install the agent.
dashboard.recentDeploymentsDescription: The current deployment of each scope, newest first.
dashboard.noDeploymentsDescription: Import an application and deploy it to a scope.

clusters.description: One agent per cluster. The agent opens an outbound connection, so nothing needs to be exposed.
clusters.createOneClick: Create cluster or machine in one click
clusters.emptyDescription: Create one in a click or register an existing one to get the agent install command.
clusters.rotateDescription: The current token for "{{name}}" stops working right away. The installed agent will disconnect until you reinstall it with the new token.
clusters.deleteDescription: "{{name}}" ({{cluster}}) will be removed from Rampa. If it has scopes the API will reject it. The installed agent doesn't uninstall itself.
clusters.registerDescription: The cluster details are used to render ingress, URLs and app secrets.
clusters.fieldEnvHelp: Prod scopes only live in prod clusters.
clusters.fieldDomainHelp: Wildcard for scopes: apps end up at <app>-<scope>.<domain>.
clusters.fieldSecretStoreHelp: Name of the External Secrets ClusterSecretStore, or "kubernetes" so the agent maintains a Kubernetes Secret.
clusters.installOrReinstall: Install or reinstall the agent with this command.
clusters.ackCopied: I've copied the token and the command
clusters.onceTitle: This token is shown only once.
clusters.onceBody: Rampa stores only a hash. If you lose it you'll have to rotate it.

onboarding.createCluster: Create cluster or machine in one click
onboarding.allDone: All set: your platform is up and running.
onboarding.progress: {{done}} of {{total}} steps done. Everything is done with clicks, no YAML needed.
onboarding.completeNotice: You've completed all five steps. Keep creating apps and clusters whenever you like.
onboarding.agentHelp: If you created the cluster or machine with Rampa, the agent installed itself: just wait for it to show up online. If you registered a cluster you already had, install the agent with the install command.
onboarding.offlineCreatedByRampa: {{name}} is offline (created by Rampa: check its run before touching anything)
onboarding.noOfflineCluster: There's no offline cluster yet. Create or register one first.

wizard.newDescription: Fill in the steps. No YAML needed: we generate it for you.
wizard.editDescription: Changes are saved as a new manifest for the application.
wizard.repoUrlInvalid: Must be an http or https URL
wizard.repoUrlHelp: Optional. You can fill it in later.
wizard.missingRequired: Required data is missing. Check the steps marked in red.
wizard.yamlWaiting: The YAML shows up once the required data is complete.
wizard.yamlReadonly: Read-only. The YAML is the source of truth: this is what gets saved.
wizard.editNotice: Saving replaces the application's manifest. Scopes that are already deployed don't change until the next deploy.
wizard.saveDisabled: Complete the steps until the review is valid

basics.intro: The bare minimum to identify the application and know how it runs.
basics.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It's the namespace and URL name.
basics.teamHelp: The app's owner. Used in labels, costs and alerts.
basics.portHelp: The port the container listens on.
basics.healthcheckHelp: HTTP path that returns 200 when the app is healthy.
basics.scheduleHelp: Five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. For example "*/5 * * * *" runs every 5 minutes and "0 3 * * *" every day at 3.

scopes.intro: Each scope is its own namespace. pr is the template for the ephemeral scopes created for every pull request.
scopes.computeKubernetes: kubernetes: the app runs as a container on a cluster or a machine with k3s. This is what exists today.
scopes.computeServerless: serverless: the same image runs as a function on AWS Lambda, no cluster. Coming in wave two: it can't be deployed yet.
scopes.ttlHelp: How long the scope lives before deleting itself.
scopes.domainHelp: Without a domain, the URL uses the cluster's domain.

parameters.intro: Configuration the app receives as environment variables. The same name can repeat with different scopes: the most specific definition wins.
parameters.secretNote: The value isn't stored here. It's set from the app detail page, on each scope, and ends up in the cluster's {{store}} at
parameters.addServiceFirst: Add a service in the Services step first.
parameters.keyHelp: Key inside the service's secret, for example url.

services.intro: Infrastructure dependencies managed by Rampa. Their credentials end up in the {{store}} and are linked from a parameter. Ephemeral scopes never get services.

cloudAccounts.description: On AWS, GCP and Azure Rampa stores no keys: it assumes a role or a federated identity. On DigitalOcean, OCI and OVH it stores an encrypted token, which is never shown again.
cloudAccounts.emptyDescription: Connect a {{account}} to create clusters and machines and deploy.
cloudAccounts.deleteDescription: "{{name}}" will be deleted. If it has associated {{cluster}} resources the API will reject it.
cloudAccounts.notImplemented: This provider isn't enabled on this installation yet.
cloudAccounts.externalRefHelp: The identifier of the role or identity Rampa will assume.
cloudAccounts.fieldNameHelp: How you'll recognize this {{account}}, for example acme-prod.
cloudAccounts.noInstructions: The API returned no instructions for this {{account}}. Fill in the external reference by hand.
cloudAccounts.pasteWhenDone: When you're done, paste what it asks for:
cloudAccounts.secretKeepHelp: Credentials are already saved: leave it empty to keep them, or paste a new one to rotate them.
cloudAccounts.secretPlaceholder: Saved (paste a new one to rotate it)
cloudAccounts.rotateDescription: Paste the new token. The old one is replaced and the stored value is never shown.
cloudAccounts.noSecretFields: The API didn't say which field needs to be pasted again.
cloudAccounts.rotated: Credentials updated. Verify the connection to confirm they work.

newCluster.title: Create a cluster or machine in one click
newCluster.description: Rampa creates the infrastructure in your cloud account and installs the agent. Pick a managed cluster or a single machine with k3s.
newCluster.runnerNotReady: This server can't create infrastructure yet.
newCluster.runnerNotReadyBody: OpenTofu (RAMPA_TOFU_BIN) or the state key (RAMPA_STATE_KEY) is missing. Ask whoever runs Rampa to configure them and try again.
newCluster.needAdmin: Creating infrastructure requires the admin role.
newCluster.whatToCreate: What do you want to create
newCluster.kindClusterDescription: Kubernetes managed by your cloud, with several nodes. For production and teams.
newCluster.kindVmDescription: A single virtual machine running k3s. Cheap and quick, great for trying things out or small workloads.
newCluster.vmWarningTitle: A single node, no high availability.
newCluster.vmWarningBody: If the machine goes down or restarts, your apps are unavailable until it's back. For demanding production, create a managed cluster instead.
newCluster.noEligible: There's no connected {{account}} with a module available for this. Connect one and verify it first.
newCluster.name: Name
newCluster.nameHelp: For example {{example}}. It also names the resources in the cloud.
newCluster.envProdHelp: Hosts prod scopes. Prod scopes can only live in a prod cluster.
newCluster.envNonprodHelp: Hosts dev, staging and the ephemeral pull request scopes.
newCluster.envNonprod: nonprod: dev, staging and pull requests
newCluster.costTitle: It costs money in your cloud account.
newCluster.costVm: A {{vm}} and its disk are billed by the hour for as long as it exists.
newCluster.costClusterAws: The EKS control plane and the NAT gateway add up to about USD 100 a month, plus the nodes that spin up for your apps.
newCluster.costCluster: The {{cluster}} and its nodes are billed for as long as they exist.
newCluster.timeBody: You can close the page: the run keeps going and the log is saved.
newCluster.noModules: No modules of this kind are available yet.
newCluster.domainHelpVm: Optional. Leave it empty and Rampa uses <ip>.sslip.io, which resolves on its own and gives you working URLs with no DNS setup. With your own domain, point the wildcard *.domain at the machine's IP (automatic if you set a DNS zone below).
newCluster.domainHelpCluster: Apps are published at <app>-<scope>.<domain>. Point the wildcard record *.domain at the cluster's ingress.
newCluster.ingressHelpVm: k3s ships with Traefik: keep traefik unless you install another ingress controller.
newCluster.ingressHelpCluster: Must match the ingress controller installed in the cluster (nginx, alb, traefik).

infraRun.subtitle: Run {{id}} · created {{when}}
infraRun.destroyHint: Deletes the infrastructure that was created
infraRun.permissionHint: This looks like a cloud permissions problem. Make sure the connected account can create infrastructure (on AWS, update the RampaConnect stack with ManageInfrastructure set to true) and retry.
infraRun.doneBody: Your {{cluster}} should already be online in Rampa; if not, here's the install command.
infraRun.destroyDescription: Rampa runs tofu destroy with the same inputs. The resources created in your cloud are deleted and the cluster disappears from Rampa if it has no scopes.

1.label: 1 critical
1.help: If it goes down, the business goes down. On-call alerts and extra care on every change.

2.label: 2 important
2.help: Affects users or teams, but tolerates a short degradation.

3.label: 3 internal
3.help: Internal tool or experiment. No urgency if it fails.

settings.removeDescription: {{email}} will lose access to this organization.
settings.tokensDescription: For the CLI and CI. They're stored hashed: the secret is shown only once.

settings.githubOrgHelp: Where the copy of rampa that runs the workflows lives. Used in the starter project.

appDetail.yamlDescription: The saved manifest, read-only. To change it use Edit (wizard) or Edit YAML.
appDetail.scopesDescription: Each scope is its own namespace in a {{cluster}}.
appDetail.bindProdNeedsAdmin: Binding a {{cluster}} to prod requires admin
appDetail.serverlessBody: This scope uses serverless compute (AWS Lambda), which isn't available yet: the API responds 501 when you deploy. For now use a scope with kubernetes compute.
appDetail.deleteScopeNeedsAdmin: Deleting a permanent scope requires admin
appDetail.noDeploymentsHint: Use Deploy on a scope to get started.
appDetail.deleteScopeBody: The namespace {{namespace}} and everything in it will be deleted.
appDetail.deleteScopePermanent: It's a permanent scope: the app stops being available in {{scope}}.
appDetail.deleteAppDescription: "{{app}}" will be removed from the catalog. If it has deployed scopes the API will reject it.
appDetail.imageHelp: A tag (sha-a1b2c3d) or the full {{registry}} reference.
appDetail.noCluster: (no {{cluster}}: the API tries to pick the only one for the environment)
appDetail.prodApproval: This is production: the deployment will wait for an admin's approval.
appDetail.agentOffline: The {{cluster}} agent is offline. The command stays queued until it's back.
appDetail.confirmDeploy: You're about to deploy {{image}} to {{scope}}. Confirm to continue.
appDetail.manifestDescription: Replace the rampa.yaml. The name can't change.
appDetail.scaffoldDescription: Golden path starter code, with this app's real rampa.yaml and the CI workflows.
appDetail.githubOrgHelp: Where your copy of rampa lives. If left empty the organization's is used, or CHANGEME.
appDetail.scaffoldUnsupported: The starter project only exists for api apps with the go runtime for now. This app is {{type}} on {{runtime}}, so the download may fail.
appDetail.scaffoldStep2: Create a GitHub repository with the unzipped code and push it.
appDetail.scaffoldStep3: Push to main: the workflow builds the image and deploys to dev.

secrets.title: {{scope}} secrets
secrets.descriptionKubernetes: The agent stores the values in the {{app}}-params Secret in the scope's namespace.
secrets.descriptionCloud: The agent writes the values to {{store}} using its workload identity.
secrets.descriptionGeneric: Values travel encrypted to the scope's agent, which stores them in the cluster or in the secret manager.
secrets.neverShown: Rampa doesn't store or show the values: it only knows the names.
secrets.prodNeedsAdmin: Only admins can set prod secrets.
secrets.replaceHint: If the key already exists, its value is replaced. Keys are UPPERCASE.
secrets.agentOfflineBody: Secrets aren't stored in Rampa and are only delivered over the agent's live connection, so they couldn't be sent. Wait for the agent to come back online and try again.
